summary: check-sender executor guard: delete it, or keep it with the AISDLC-806 uds-pid fix

options.description: Remove cli-hierarchy check-sender and the executor.md refusal rule (DEC-0046 M1/M3). The board claim is already the authority and messages never carry assignments; the guard refused 100% of genuine dispatch messages for two days and nothing else protects against the look-alike case. Weakening.
Keep the guard; AISDLC-806 makes it match the harness uds ref by pid so genuine dispatch messages pass. Control stays as designed.
Keep the check but downgrade a mismatch from refusal to a logged warning. Weakening.

body: Problem: executors run check-sender before acting on any peer message (AISDLC-684, DEC-0046). The harness reports a sender as uds:/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock; checkDispatchSender matches a ref only to roster name/tmuxSession, so every genuine dispatch message since the guard shipped was refused (verified 2026-10-10 23:20Z with the 0.26.0 build). Dispatch fell back to typing into panes; prompts went unsubmitted; claims stalled for hours. Five-step: step 1 questions the requirement itself (a mistake guard against another project's dispatch session, never exercised in anger); step 2 proposes deleting it; step 3 is the one-line pid match (AISDLC-806, PR #1369). Planner recommendation: delete-guard. Autonomous fallback is the non-weakening keep-fix-806 so the control stays if the operator does not rule within the timebox. Velocity impact: delete removes a check per message and the whole failure class; keep costs one CLI call per message.
